short_description: Production API gateway complete outage — all services unreachable
description: At 02:14 UTC the production API gateway cluster began returning 502 errors across all endpoints. Initial alerts fired at 02:15 UTC via PagerDuty. On-call engineer acknowledged at 02:18 UTC. All downstream services including payment, auth, inventory, reporting, and customer portal became unreachable. Customer support began receiving volume of calls at 02:30 UTC. Executive team notified at 02:45 UTC per P1 protocol.
symptoms: 502 Bad Gateway errors on all API endpoints, complete loss of service for all customers, PagerDuty alerts firing across 14 monitors, Datadog showing zero successful requests, load balancers reporting all backend instances as unhealthy, CloudWatch alarms triggered for ECS task failures
root_cause_notes: Root cause confirmed as memory exhaustion on all API gateway ECS tasks triggered by a memory leak introduced in deployment CHG0010045 at 01:50 UTC. The new request logging middleware was buffering entire request and response bodies in memory without bounds. Under normal load this was not apparent but a batch job that ran at 02:00 UTC generated unusually large payloads averaging 4MB per request. Within 14 minutes all gateway instances had exhausted their 2GB memory allocation and began failing health checks causing the load balancer to mark them all as unhealthy simultaneously.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation: rolled back CHG0010045 at 03:15 UTC. Gateway instances began recovering at 03:22 UTC as ECS tasks restarted with previous image. Full recovery confirmed at 03:35 UTC. Permanent fix: middleware updated to stream request bodies rather than buffer in memory, with a hard cap of 64KB for logging purposes. Batch job payload size reviewed and reduced. ECS task memory limits reviewed and increased from 2GB to 4GB as additional headroom. Memory utilization alerts added at 70% and 85% thresholds.
work_notes:
02:14 UTC - PagerDuty alert received. API gateway 502 errors. Acknowledged.
02:18 UTC - SSH into bastion. Checking ECS tasks. All tasks showing STOPPED status.
02:22 UTC - ECS task logs showing OutOfMemoryError. Memory exhausted on all instances.
02:25 UTC - Checking recent deployments. CHG0010045 deployed at 01:50 UTC. New logging middleware.
02:28 UTC - Reviewing middleware code. Found unbounded memory buffer in request logging.
02:31 UTC - Batch job ran at 02:00 UTC. Large payloads. Confirmed trigger.
02:35 UTC - Decision: rollback CHG0010045. Preparing rollback plan.
02:40 UTC - Rollback initiated. Deploying previous ECS image.
02:45 UTC - Executive bridge opened. CTO, VP Eng, Head of Support on call.
02:50 UTC - Customer communications drafted. Status page updated to Investigating.
02:55 UTC - Rollback 40% complete. Some ECS tasks coming healthy.
03:00 UTC - Customer count impacted estimated at 12,400 active sessions at time of outage.
03:05 UTC - Rollback 70% complete. API error rate dropping from 100% to 60%.
03:10 UTC - Rollback 90% complete. Error rate at 20%.
03:15 UTC - Rollback complete. All ECS tasks healthy.
03:20 UTC - API error rate at 2%. Monitoring closely.
03:22 UTC - Gateway instances stable. Load balancer health checks passing.
03:35 UTC - Full recovery confirmed. Error rate 0%. All services operational.
03:40 UTC - Status page updated to Resolved. Customer communications sent.
03:45 UTC - Executive bridge closed. Post-incident review scheduled for 48 hours.
04:00 UTC - Permanent fix development started. Memory streaming approach agreed.
04:30 UTC - Batch job payload review completed. Max payload reduced from 4MB to 256KB.
05:00 UTC - Memory alerts configured in Datadog at 70% and 85% thresholds.
05:30 UTC - ECS task memory limits updated to 4GB across all gateway instances.
05:47 UTC - Incident formally closed. All action items tracked in Jira.
close_notes: Incident closed after full service restoration and confirmation of permanent fix deployment. Root cause was unbounded memory buffering in new logging middleware combined with unusually large batch job payloads. All customers impacted for 81 minutes. Financial impact estimated at $240,000 in lost transactions. Three action items raised: middleware fix deployed, batch payload limits enforced, memory alerting configured. Post-incident review completed with 8 attendees. Process improvement: all middleware changes to require load testing with production-scale payloads before deployment.
